utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: If Your Honour would like me to address the archive issue a bit more, then I should be in a better position to do. But we can do that later or maybe we don't need to address it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, let's see how the evidence progresses first of all. Good afternoon, Mr. Zyrapi.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The evidence will resume again. As always, the solemn declaration to tell the truth continues to apply to your evidence. Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, I want to talk to you now about statements you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor. The first statement that I'm aware of was one you gave over a two-day period on the 22nd of November, 2005, and then again on the 25th of November, 2005. And according to my information, this was given in the Pristina field office of the OTP. Is that all correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And that's the same office that you delivered these documents from the archives to when you took them in, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And do you remember that the persons who interviewed you were named Ole Lehtinen and Philippe Vallieres-Roland?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And did you ever have any contact with either of them other than these two days when you were interviewed?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And they were both from the Office of the Prosecutor, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's how they interviewed themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And there was an interpreter there to assist with the language issue. Was anyone else there? Was it just you and those three persons?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my recollection, these were the only persons that were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right. Now, the -- the interviews took place on -- during this week, on a Tuesday and on a Friday. The 22nd was a Tuesday and the 25th was a Friday. What happened on Wednesday and Thursday? I mean, why weren't you interviewed on those two days instead of carrying over then until the Friday?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. It was working days, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. Okay. I just want -- I don't want to spend a lot of time on this, but I would like to just find out from you exactly how this statement was taken. Were they typing -- were they typing what you were saying while they were speaking to you? Is that the way this statement was prepared, or was it prepared in a different way or do you know?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To what I know, they wrote down the statement that I was giving.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And there was a time, wasn't there, I guess on the 25th, when you were presented with a typewritten copy of it that you were asked to review and sign. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on that day I signed my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And I take it that while this statement was given it wasn't being recorded or anything like that; they were just making notes of what you were saying. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they recorded it as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: An audio-recording or what?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Audio-recording, yes. There was an audio-recording equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the second statement on the 6th of July that you gave here at The Hague, it indicated that Jonathan Sutch and Keith Scully were the people who interviewed you at that time. Was it pretty much done the same way?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I gave the second statement in July, the computer was there. They were typing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if it was recorded or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right. All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters kindly request for the witness to speak up. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, you're being asked by the interpreters if you could speak up a little. If you just sit back -- just sit back from the microphone and speak just a little bit more loudly. Mr. Ackerman, is there a point related to these statements?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm finished with them, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But what's the point of this?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I didn't think we had ever really established in this Tribunal the method by which these statements were taken, the complete method, so I just wanted to get that in the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: For what it's worth, which may be nothing, Your Honour, in the final analysis, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like you to look at Exhibit P2449 again. You've seen this before. These are the -- the interim regulations of the KLA that you brought to us, and I'm interested in the first page of that right after the title page. And we'll get to that next page I think in just a second. And you told us in your testimony the other day that this document was -- was updated. You were asked by Mr. Marcussen at page 5945 of the transcript: "To your knowledge, was this document updated since the version that we're looking at now?" And you said: "Yes, with the passage of time we made changes to it. We updated it. Like, for example, the greetings, the saluting, and other things which time required us to change depending on the further developments and growth of the KLA." I'm wondering why you brought us a version that was basically out of date instead of -- of the updated version, which might be more relevant to what we're doing here.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only had this version. I couldn't find the other version.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now, you talked about this version having been produced in large quantities and distributed all throughout the KLA down to as low as the squad level; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know it was printed out and distributed to the zones, and then it was the responsibility of the zones to distribute it to lower levels.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And apparently that didn't happen with the updated versions or you wouldn't have had so much difficulty finding it, if it was produced in such large quantity; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. The changes that were made in the new versions were distributed to lower levels, but I don't know how many copies remained.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. Well, when you -- when you answered Mr. Marcussen's question about updates, you didn't say anything about the oath; but then when Mr. Petrovic asked you about the oath, you said that also had been changed, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now, the -- the oath that's contained in this document that you've provided us contains this language, and you'll see it there on your screen: "As a member of the Kosovo Liberation Army, I swear that I will fight for the liberation of the occupied territories of Albania and their unification." That language certainly appears there, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now, is that the oath that you took when you became a member of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I became a member of the KLA, I didn't take this oath.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Did you take any oath?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I joined the KLA, I of course gave a statement that I joined the KLA. That statement was approved by the General Staff, and that's how I became a member.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: This military oath that's contained in this document, if you look at paragraph 3 a little further down the page, it says that -- it's an act of particular significance in the life of every soldier. And paragraph 4 it's to be taken before the flag and that the officer who gives the oath, there in paragraph 6 you'll see - I think that's probably the next page in the Albanian document - that the officer is supposed to read the text and interrupt him so he can repeat what he says in unison. So according to this, it's treated pretty seriously, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now, what do you think would happen if -- if one of the KLA recruits refused to take that oath and said, I'm not interested in the liberation of the occupied territories of Albania and their unification. I just want to join the KLA to defend my village. I guess he wouldn't be permitted to be part of the KLA, would he?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. There weren't such cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Could we look --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: There weren't such cases. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Could we look, please, at P2469 now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Another one of the maps that you're familiar with.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And if we could just blow it up just a little bit and go down toward the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now, what I want to ask you, and you may not know, but I want to ask you if you can show us on this map what the occupied territories of Albania were, as this oath speaks of. And clearly that must have included Kosovo, but apparently also parts of Macedonia and Montenegro. Can you outline those parts for us and maybe part of Serbia. Can you -- can you find them on this map and maybe draw a line around them or something, so we can see what parts of all these countries the KLA was fighting for?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already stated that as they have envisaged it earlier, it should comprise of territories inhabited by Albanian majority.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: But you don't know what those territories are? Oh, yeah, you're drawing it now. Okay.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Let me ask you something -- now it's too late. Go ahead, draw your lines as best you can.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the time I was in office, this was not the case, but I'm just drawing the line how it could have been imagined.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I think maybe we're not going to get the result we want with this map blown up like this, so let's start over again and put the map back -- a fresh one on the page and focus on the upper right-hand corner. And maybe with that little map in the upper right-hand corner blown up, you'll be able to do a better job. We'll see if you can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: If we just put this map on without blowing it, you'll have the whole area, will you not?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, that may be true, Your Honour. We can try that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Let's bring it back to its normal size.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay. Now, try to do it now the way it is. We just have the map on the screen.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you want me to draw the line?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said earlier, when I joined the KLA, this was not the case. But this is what was imagined.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do you mean to include in this area any part of Bulgaria?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So where the right-hand boundary is in fairly rough terms, you mean it to run in line with the boundary of Kosovo, do you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry. It's my mistake. I'm sorry. I'm misreading the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: How about Greece? Is any part of Greece included in this concept of occupied territories of Albania?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not during my time in office.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Could we have that photographed and made an exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be IC107, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now, I want to put 2449 back on the screen. We may not need it, but just in case.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Sir, do you remember, without looking at it, that this set of regulations you gave us has a chapter 1 and a chapter 2. And then if you turn to the page, it goes to chapter 5. Do you remember that? Chapter 3 and 4 are missing.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't remember. What I could find, I brought it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And I take it you don't remember what chapters 3 and 4 were about?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And then there's also no chapter -- well, maybe -- all right. Now, you said that one of the things that was changed was saluting. In chapter 5, Roman numeral IV, number 4, I don't know if the registrar can get us to that point or not. I'll just read you what the translation says. "Military saluting is carried out with the arm stretched out." And then you told us that that -- the new version changed "saluting." It's paragraph IV under number 4. You have to go up I think and back a page, maybe. Can you tell us what was changed if the salute originally was carried out with the arm stretched out -- maybe you can demonstrate for us what that meant. Was it stretched out to the side or to the front? How was the armed stretched out in this salute?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in the beginning, the saluting was with the right-hand side with a fist, and then it changed into a stretched hand. You put your right hand close to your head, and that's how you salute.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So would you look at me. At first it was with the fist and off to the side of your body like this or up like this or to your head like this? Why don't you do it so we can see it.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the beginning it was with a fist, like this, and later it changed into a stretched hand like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay. To describe what you're doing. You've got your arm crooked with your fist against your right temple, and then you've got your palm outstretched with the tips of your fingers touching your right temple. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman, is there any purpose in this cross-examination? It would help me if you could tell me where we're going with it to understand its significance.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm trying to figure out what saluting carried out with the arm stretched out is. The only time I've seen such a salute it looked like this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Indeed that's what it sounds like in the translation if it's an accurate translation. But what's the point in the case? Help me on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I was wondering if there might not have been some kind of fascist influence in the original KLA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So what?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, it might tell you something about the character of the organisation, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You don't think there's been loads of evidence about that already?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I think there's been quite a bit, yes. I'm finished with that. I now have one final question on this document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, if you think it's relevant, what I'd like to see is the Albanian version of this translated by the witness, so that we can hear whether it's the hand of the arm that's referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That would be fine with me. It's not on the screen yet, but it could be if we go down one number. It's number 4. It's the next number down.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I think you have to go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It's the top of the next page then. Well, I don't know how that was even translated.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Sir, can you read what it says there, the top line.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not very clear, the copy. "Military saluting is done through outstretched hand," it says, but the copied part is not legible.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There's -- it seems a fairly significant translation difficulty if the word is "hand" and not "arm."

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Yes, but the witness is primarily here to testify, to establish whether or not there was an armed conflict of an internal nature and the structure of the KLA and those sorts of things. But yes, there is a problem there, but getting back to the relevance here of the cross I guess.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, of course the witness is not confined to the purpose for which the Prosecution may have brought him. But this -- this is what -- is this a CLSS translation?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I think so, yes, but I would have to check.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, we'll have it checked I think, although whether they can work with the copy or not, I don't know. But the court deputy will raise that and we'll get a report, which we'll circulate. Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Sorry. My well-informed case manager tells me that from the way the document -- the translation is numbered, it can be seen that it is an official translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Under chapter VII, paragraph 3, and then at numbered paragraph 4, the regulation provided that: "Soldiers must be given enough time to rest so they're not tired while at the positions." Was that ever changed or did that stay as part of the regulations?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It remained the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry for those little delays, but if I don't touch my computer for half an hour it quits me, and then I don't have a transcript to watch. All right. I'm finished with that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I want to ask you about a couple of people. Who is Adem Demaqi?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Adem Demaqi was a spokesperson of the KLA during the war. Before the war, he was imprisoned for political reasons, and after the war, I don't know what he is engaged in. But I know that during the war he was a KLA spokesperson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And during that time in 1999, during the war when he was the KLA spokesperson, did he have any particular authority? Was he able to make decisions and things of that nature, or did he just speak for those who could make decisions?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He worked for the political directorate. I cannot tell you what powers he had.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: What about Fehmi Agani, do you know about what role he played in 1988/1989 [sic], before he died?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not he had a great deal of influence with the KLA or control over the KLA?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, during the time I was serving, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Ibrahim Rugova, you certainly know who that is. Did he have a lot of influence and control over the KLA?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, no. Maybe the political directorate is better positioned to tell you, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Did you ever encounter a person by the name of Ratomir Tanic?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, page 13, line 17 should say "1998" and "1999," not "1988" and "1989."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Do you have any reason to believe that Ibrahim Rugova and Fehmi Agani were influential in Kosovo and able to control radical elements in the political landscape?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said earlier, I never dealt with political affairs and I can't tell you whether he had an influence on political issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: To your knowledge, though, those persons were not influential in that regard, as far as you know? You have no information that they were?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I hope I don't have to go through putting a document on the screen, but I will if I have to. In the bottom left part of most of the documents which you brought with you, there are some capital letters. On some of the documents you'll see SV/AM, some you'll see SS/SS. Do you have any idea what those mean?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the persons who has printed these documents or the persons who typed these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right. In your testimony, during direct examination, at page 5941, lines 11 through 13, you gave us this information: "In September of 1998 I left Kosovo and went to Albania on a duty trip assigned by the staff and I stayed there until November, when I went back to Kosovo." What kind of a duty trip was it that took you to Albania for two months?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time when I went to Albania in September, I had the duty of -- of re-organising the formations of the KLA, because after the summer offensive, many of the units were broken up and many people left. So I had to recruit experienced cadres to join the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So you were recruiting and organising and training in Albania?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And the people you were recruiting and training and organising were not necessarily persons from Kosovo but persons from Albania and other parts of the world?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were Albanians from Kosova. The higher officers were former JNA officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, there were Albanians from Albania and from the United States and from Switzerland, Germany, elsewhere that were also part of the KLA, weren't there?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said even earlier that Albanians came from several countries of Europe where they used to live.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And you had Albanians from Albania as part of the KLA, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were some, but not many.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: What was the Atlantic Brigade?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Atlantic Brigade, at that time when I left, September, October, November, wasn't in existence. It started its operation in 1999, and it was made up of Albanians who lived in the United States, Australia, and other countries.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes. Now, this -- this recruiting and training and so forth that you were doing in Albania, this certainly was with the approval and assistance of the Albanian government, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we talk about this Atlantic Brigade and other brigades, at that time we used some places which we were allowed to use. This was for training.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And you were getting assistance from the Government of Albania and the people of Albania also, weren't you? Weapons were being supplied by Albania?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What period are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, you were there between September and November, that period, when you were there and could observe it personally.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't have any assistance from the Albanian government during that period in regard to what you me about.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: What period did you have that assistance?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That assistance -- the assistance was after the bombing started.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay. The KLA soldiers, there were women who were part of the KLA, weren't there?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And they were similarly armed and wore similar uniforms to the men, did they not?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Most of them had uniforms, but most of them worked in logistics.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right. I want to go to some testimony you gave during direct again. Page 5959, lines 12 through 17, Mr. Marcussen asked you this: "I would like to now move into sort of more practical structure of the KLA and moving down to the bottom of the organisation, so to speak. How many soldiers did the KLA have during the time you were Chief of Staff?" And you answered: "During the time I was Chief of Staff until March 1999, the KLA had approximately 17.000 to 18.000 soldiers in the territory of Kosova." Now, after March of 1999, did that number increase even more?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I have no information about that, but to my knowledge the number increased.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now, these 17 to 18.000 soldiers that you have knowledge about, just some practical questions. Were there military posts or barracks where these soldiers were housed and fed?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In general, we didn't have barracks everywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Was that your entire answer?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, it seemed to me like -- he's speaking so softly, I have trouble knowing whether he's talking or not. It seems to me like he gave a very long answer and we get a very short translation. Maybe I missed it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note that we have problems following him, too. He speaks very low.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Sir, can you speak more loudly so the interpreters can hear you. And I'm going to ask you the question again just to make sure we get the answer. Were there military posts or barracks where these 17 or 18.000 soldiers were housed and fed?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: For a large number, yes; for the remainder, no. I mean here the logistics, the political staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Where did these soldiers sleep? Where did they spend the nights if they weren't in barracks?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In general, they were stationed in schools, in facilities, collective facilities, in houses, depending on the situation and the region.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, I know that Ramush Haradinaj, for instance, had his headquarters in his family compound. Were there a lot of the compounds that soldiers were quartered in where they would spend the nights at least?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said "depending on the situation," the territories, the circumstances, there were and there were not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And I take it that the -- these family compounds were -- were somewhat like fortifications in some respect and especially the kullas that could serve as defensive points and firing points and so forth. That's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I spoke about the stationing of the units, I meant the places where they rested and were fed, the fortifications.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay. But they also fought from some of these compounds with the kullas and so forth, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, no. The fortification points were far from these places.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: These -- you described the organisation of the KLA that was squads, platoons, companies, and brigades. Did the squads always remain together?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The squads, yes, depending on the terrain and the circumstances. The platoons were always near each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'd like to show you a -- we're talking about these family compounds. I'd like to show you a photograph, and we can put it on the ELMO so everybody can see it, if the usher will come get it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: If I may ask, Mr. Ackerman. Is that one of the documents that we have been notified about that's coming on?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: No, it's not because it just came up as a result of what the witness said about the compounds. I thought it'd be helpful for the Judges to see what one of these family compounds looks like in terms of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Marcussen, what -- do you oppose this?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Well, I mean, obviously the question was prepared that the questioning was going in the direction of the compounds and it wasn't coming up. It's again the Trial Chamber's order that we should be notified about these things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, do you oppose it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I oppose it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. We really should have some regulation here, Mr. Ackerman. Mr. Marcussen is objecting to this because there is an order about how we should deal with exhibits. What do you have to say? No, Mr. Ackerman, I want to hear from --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I have never seen the document until two minutes ago -- the picture until two minutes ago, when it was handed to me, because I was talking about these compounds, and it was handed to me as a representative picture of what these compounds looked like. And I thought it might be helpful to Your Honours to see a picture of what these compounds looked like. If I had known about it as early as lunchtime, I certainly would have notified the Prosecutor that I intended to use it. And I don't think it's a sneak-up on them in any way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I suppose it is one of the photographs I received directly. It may have been some three hours ago. It was disclosed by the UK government. I believe Mr. Ackerman used one of those completely new exhibits; therefore, there was no fault on his part. He wasn't trying to keep anything from the other party.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I received the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. I don't see that this is going to cause any prejudice to the Prosecution, so we'll allow it to be exhibited.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now, if it's possible just to zoom in a little bit to get it kind of -- okay. That's good enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now, sir, you see the photograph there that's in front of you I guess.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I am told that that's a family compound located where, in Gornje Prekaze. It says it right on the screen. That's the Adem Jashari family compound that's, you know, quite notorious. It's a significantly high wall around that place, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see the group of houses. This is a traditional form of houses. It's a kind of household, housing several families living together in the same compound.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this particular one, Mr. Zyrapi?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not familiar with this particular one because I was not in that territory, neither during the war or before the war. And I cannot tell you who it belongs to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Give us a number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be IC --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: We can give it an IC number, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be IC108, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And can we get it scanned or something so it goes into the system where it happened and then returned? Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now, what I was asking you about was this organisation. The lowest part of the organisation you talked about the other day were squads, and I'm just wondering if these squads remained together all the time.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The squads were together in the same place.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now, I know that there were times when people went on leave and things of that nature, so I'm -- let's exempt that from my questions, if you will. The squads were part of platoons. Did the platoons remain together at all times?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking about the time I served. The squads -- the platoons were together, depending on the territories, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, I'm talking about the time you served, too. I think you probably can't help us during the time you cannot. So I'll understand that that's what you're talking about. Now, I assume when you get up to the company and brigade level, then you start seeing some dispersement of these units. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Depending on the configuration of the terrain. As I said, most of them were stationed in the territories included in their zone of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay. I want to ask you some questions now about your statement. At the beginning of your statement you talked about your early days with the KLA, that those days you spent in Tirana. Why in Tirana and not in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've stated in my statement, I was asked by Xhemalj Fetahu to go to Tirana. When I went to Tirana, my intention was to continue to Kosovo, but Xhemalj asked me to stay there for a while, to offer them my assistance in training the soldiers that were coming to join the KLA from different countries in Europe. And I was also waiting there for the confirmation from the General Staff regarding my joining the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right. What was the FARK, the F-A-R-K?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: FARK were the armed forces of the Republic of Kosova.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And it's true, isn't it, that there was tension between the FARK and the KLA?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Exhibit P2450 - I don't know that we need to look at it - it is that document where it showed that a KLA soldier by the name of Behim Shala was issued one automatic rifle, three grenades, and 330 rounds of ammunition upon his taking the oath and becoming a soldier in the KLA. Now, this would have simply been an initial allotment of grenades and ammunition, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly, but this is the procedure followed when a soldier joins, to issue him a weapon and ammunition that could be given to him, that was at our disposal to give to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And then when there was fighting and that ammunition and those grenades were used, there would be additional ammunition and grenades issued I take it, so that that soldier could fight another day?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and additional ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And I assume that this initial allotment that's set out in that document changed over time, so sometimes there may have been less available and sometimes more?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now, I would like to look at P2453, please. And I'd like to look at the -- the second page I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: These are the minutes of that -- of that work meeting in Gllogjan and Glodjane that was talked about earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Could we look at the bottom of that page just for a moment. A little further down, please. Okay. The actual part of it I'm looking for is Smajl says at the bottom -- and with me it's page 5 which for some reason is the second page of the document in English. The speaker is Smajl, S-m-a-j-l, and he says: "To assist one another in the future, we have to supply weapons to the whole population from the age of 16." It's right there on the screen. I can see it. I can read enough Albanian to recognise the number 16 there. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Was that carried out? Did you actually go into the villages and arm the -- arm the whole population from age 16 up?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my knowledge, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I take it there was an effort made to do that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During my time, the efforts were to fill the units, but what is written here, to my knowledge, was not carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now, this person, Smajl, that was actually Ramush Haradinaj, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's a pseudonym of Ramush Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And he wound up being the commander of one of the operative zones, right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in these minutes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And he remained the commander in that operative zone, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And as the commander, if he had then ordered that weapons be supplied to the whole population from age 16 up, I take it that order would have been followed as much as possible, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if it was carried out or not.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the last part of the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your still not speaking loud enough for the interpreters to hear you. Is there any way we can get you to speak louder and then repeat that answer so we can get it all?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know to what extent it was carried out, but it couldn't have been fully carried out because it was impossible to issue weapons to everybody who was of military age and able to join the KLA units.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay. I want to go to some other issues now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Ackerman, we're at a fairly wide range in cross-examination. Now, there are other interests to be considered. I don't know to what extent they wish to cross-examine, but can we focus on what really matters to you now?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have prepared a great deal and I'm trying -- there is actually some of it I do want to skip and so I'm trying to figure out what to continue with and what not to. So I am making an effort in that regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Let me go to, at least for the moment, to some of the documents that you supplied to the OTP. And the first one I'll have brought up is Exhibit 4D40, please. All right. That document is now on the screen in front of you, and I take it you recognise that as one of the documents you got from the archives and supplied to the OTP?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And this is an order dated 10 January 1999 directed to the brigade commanders in the Pastrik zone of operation; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Signed by Ekrem Rexha, the commander of that zone?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is signed by the deputy commander as far as I can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... looks like it is, but issued under Ekrem Rexha's name at least?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the name is the name of the commander Ekrem Rexha, but the signature is the signature of his deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And if he look at the initial paragraph then up at the top again, it says it was issued pursuant to order number 94/111 of 6 January 1999. Do you have any idea what that order was?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an order sent to zone commander to secure the use of material goods and to ensure facilities where KLA units can be based.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So -- so this order that we're looking at was basically the order that came from the General Staff to the zone commanders, passed on along to the brigades. Is that a fair way to analyse it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And basically what this order does is -- is order and authorise the confiscation of vehicles from the population for use by the army, doesn't it, and specifically or preferably, Nivas and Suzukis and Land Rovers; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order specifies terrain vehicles that can be used for the needs of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: But it authorises the confiscation of these vehicles from the population, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It authorises for these all-terrain vehicles to be taken pursuant to the procedures that I have mentioned earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And it doesn't restrict that to vehicles that are owned by Kosovar Albanians, but they could be taken from Serbs or taken from Roma or anybody else that just happened to be there with a Niva or a Suzuki or a Land Rover; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order pertains to the zones that were under the KLA control.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, it would make sense that they could only seize vehicles in a zone under their control, but it doesn't restrict it to Albanian-owned vehicles. It could be Serb-owned vehicles or Roma-owned vehicles or American-owned vehicles or whatever you could get your hands on, right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The meaning of this order was to take these vehicles from the Albanians who possess these kinds of all-terrain vehicles that could be used for the needs of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, is this order confined to vehicles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not only to vehicles, also to facilities needed for the KLA units, for the stationing of KLA units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And that would be authority to take over the homes of individuals for accommodation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not homes, but facilities that are for that particular moment unpopulated and that can be used for the KLA needs. As I mentioned earlier, schools or collective facilities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, to be fair, it doesn't say anything about unpopulated or unused vehicles or anything of that nature, does it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not say "unused vehicles" or "unused facilities." Facilities that can be used. For example, buildings of different corporations that were no longer working.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, you did talk about --

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Houses that were used for schooling in the past.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You talked about unpopulated facilities, but it's not restricted to that, is it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was not restricted to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now, this -- this order that came from the General Staff down through the chain of command and out to the brigades and so forth, this order of course was not authorised by any kind of civil authority properly constituted, was it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at that time, only by the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yeah, it was just, in effect, organised theft by members of an illegal insurgency, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Argumentative, I think, Mr. Ackerman. Let's ask questions that we expect sensible answers to.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Could we look at 5891, please. Oh, I'm sorry, 4D39.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now, this is an order of 10 January of 1999 signed on behalf of Ekrem Rexha again. And what this does is pass along an order from the General Staff that brigade commanders have to register the numbers of their satellite telephones or their phones are going to be blocked; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now, I understood that satellite telephones are really pretty exotic and expensive items. It seems that the KLA had many of these if each of the brigade commanders had one. There must have been a lot of them, huh?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not all the brigades, part of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Do you know where these satellite phones came from? Do you know who supplied those to the KLA?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that. The logistics directorate, it was its duty to supply these phones.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Did you ever hear of an American Albanian by the name of Florim Krasniqi?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've heard of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Did you ever speak to him on your satellite phone?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: After the war?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the war I saw him and I met him personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay. He was a pretty significant contributor to the KLA, wasn't he, money-wise, material-wise, weapon-wise?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As many other individuals --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a matter of the logistics directorate, as I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Let's look at 4D38, please. And, Your Honour, while we're waiting for it to come up, I think I should explain to the Trial Chamber that these are some of the documents that -- that the Prosecution chose not to use that were furnished to us and we submitted to CLSS. And CLSS should be commended for getting these translated with such speed, and I certainly want to express my appreciation for that. It's helped us quite a bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: This document issued 18 January 1999, I think it's actually signed by Mr. Rexha. And this talks about raising military readiness to its highest level. Now, this was during the time of the cease-fire, was it not?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is an order that was issued during that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And it provides that military readiness should be raised to the highest level, that all soldiers outside the unit are to report to their unit, the ZOP it's called here. A platoon of military police and a liaison squad are to be kept in full military readiness, combat readiness; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only the platoon, but all units in general, the military, police unit, the intervention unit, all units in general.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And I'm curious about paragraph number 4 there. "All movements of persons unknown and uninvited in the direction of the command buildings are strictly forbidden." That was basically the general public was not permitted to approach your command buildings; is that what that's saying?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And paragraph 5 says that nobody can go on leave during this period of high alert state.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Do you have any idea what was going on in the Pastrik Operational Zone on 18 January 1999 during a cease-fire to justify this kind of high-level readiness?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my recollection, at that time there wasn't an increased movement in Pashtrik zone, rather in Nerodime zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay. Now, during your testimony on direct, you were asked about the military equipment, basically the weaponry, that was available to the KLA. And I don't recall that you mentioned 120-millimetre rocket-launchers during that, did you?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did mention it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Those were the mortars basically that you were talking about, or were those the Katyusha?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the mortars.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay. So those can be referred to as rocket-launchers?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, 120-millimetre mortars, as it is mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, I'm wondering about 120-millimetre rocket-launchers. Do you know what those are?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about 120-millimetre rocket-launchers, but I do know about 120-millimetre mortars.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So to your knowledge there was no such thing as 120-millimetre rocket-launchers available to the KLA?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. There weren't any at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right. And the other one I want to ask you about is, I don't think you mentioned any anti-aircraft weapons, did you?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And I guess there weren't any anti-aircraft weapons available to the KLA either?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Except for two M-Strelas which were not in working order.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'd like you to look at another document, 4D37. Now, this is a document dated 3 February of 1999 signed by a commander named Sulejman Selimi. And he's wanting an artillery officer named Enver Rrustemin to train users of 120-millimetre rocket-launchers and to have officer Kurtish Fane to train people to utilise the Strela 2 anti-aircraft equipment. Now, that wouldn't make any sense if there weren't any 120-millimetre rocket-launchers or if the Strela 2 anti-aircraft equipment wasn't functioning, would it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order is very clear. It's not signed by Sylejman Selimi, but by another officer. The word "minahedhsa," it refers to mortars, not to rocket-launchers. And as for the Strela-2 M, there were two pieces of this kind of weaponry but they were not in working order.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, I know you've said that, but why would he want somebody to train somebody how to use them if they didn't work. It doesn't make any sense, does it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, regardless of whether these weapons were available or not to us, the training had to take place of all kinds of collective weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'd like you to read after the name Enver Rrustemin, I'd like you to just read the language right after that starting with the word that looks like per, p-e-r. Just read that down to the next name because I'd like to hear the translation.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The training of those who will serve there for mine launchers 120 millimetres and the officer Kurtish Fane, to be trained to use the anti-aircraft M Stella-2, the sending of these officers by you is necessary."

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have another translation issue I guess.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, we didn't get the answer to the question you are asking. Please read that again, Mr. Zyrapi.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. "For the training of people who will use mine launchers 120-millimetres and the officer Kurtish Fane, to use the anti-aircraft Strela-2. Dispatch of these officers by you is necessary, is urgent."

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think -- I've heard it twice now. I think what is being interpreted is the word mine, m-i-n-e, launchers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: But it's not showing up in the transcript. It is now, of course, since I've said it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That would sound like a mortar rather than a rocket-launcher.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes, that's exactly what it is. That's another translation issue with regard to this document. Because it does say -- the English translation does say rocket-launchers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And rocket-launchers are frequently referred to in evidence and perhaps we should be cautious about the language when such expressions are used. Can I ask you where we are now because we're about to have a break?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to suggest we take a break now and give me a chance to go over my notes and I may or may not have any additional questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Just one thing I think I should address before the break, but it doesn't have to be at this very moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, no, what is it you wish to address?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: In light of the witness's evidence about his first interview being recorded, we have checked our evidence and regrettably there exists a transcript of that conversation which has not been disclosed. I have it. It's Albanian and translated into English. I haven't had the time to review it and compare it to the statement. But I think obviously this is something we'll immediately disclose to the Defence, and we'll have to figure out how to do that, if it gives rise to further cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, do you have questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I have quite a few questions, but I will also try to reduce them as much as possible and to use all the time you allot to me as best I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Same situation as with Mr. Cepic, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: As you know, we're trying not to get into the territory of very precise allocations of time. We've given guidance. But there is an issue of fairness arises where the Defence cross-examination is largely the development of a positive case rather than a challenge to the Prosecution case, and we have to look at how to you deal with that. Because when we get to the Defence case, it's actually quite difficult to make the same allowances. And it may be that one way of doing this is to bear in mind the situation where a lot of the cross is the positive presentation of a Defence case. And to actually allocate that time in due course against the Defence case when it comes to be presented. Now, I'm not making -- I'm thinking aloud at the moment because this is the first time we've encountered this particular difficulty, and I don't think at this stage, in any event, we could make such a decision. We would have to make such a decision in the proper context, having regard to the fairness to the parties. But it may be that that is the way to do it. And if you see that as a way forward, then it actually relieves us of having to determine cut-off points for cross-examination where you genuinely believe this is necessary cross-examination in the interests of the presentation of your case, but really have to accept that at some stage you'll have to have it counted against you rather than simply have an open-ended cheque. It's one of the problems of allocating time that we can do it specifically for the party who's presenting the case, but we can't really do it terribly precisely for the cross-examining party.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I -- that is a -- that's an excellent observation I think, and that's -- that's exactly what's going on and it's motived a great deal by -- you know, I know you have some strong feelings about this, but it's motived a great deal by the proposition that it's extraordinarily difficult for us to interview witnesses in Kosovo, to find witnesses in Kosovo, and to bring witnesses here from Kosovo. So when we get a witness who we can kind of use as a witness to present our case, we'd be remiss in not using. Because I don't think we could ever get a high officer of the KLA to come here to testify for the Defence. I don't think that could ever happen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But you understand the need that the Trial Chamber has to make sure that both sides are treated fairly in this, and that at the end of this trial, both sides have had an equal opportunity to present their respective cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I do, and I think your suggestion makes sense because if I could call a witness to get the evidence that I'm wanting to get from this witness, I'd be using the time in my Defence case. So when I'm using it now it probably makes sense.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I imagine it's better to cross-examine than to bring your own witness in the first place. So you've got an additional advantage there. But having made these remarks, it's also necessary to retain an overall control over the total time used for the presentation of the Prosecution case. So this is not an invitation to you to take an open-ended approach to every witness from whom you might see some benefit for the Defence, the positive presentation of the Defence case. It's going to be a very delicate balancing exercise. I simply ask you to have this in mind so when we do eventually have to made hard decisions, that you've had an adequate opportunity to consider the options. Mr. Zyrapi, we have our break now. The usher will again show you where to wait and we'll resume at 4.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, I'm going to ask you some questions about some incidents that I understand occurred in Kosovo and ask you if you're familiar at all with the incidents and can give us any further information than what I have about them. If you're not familiar with the incident, you can just say you know nothing about it and we can move to the next question, and thereby save some time. Okay? Did you hear me?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. I have some information that I'm told came from the Government of the United States, and it's reported that on the 21st of November, 1998, the KLA held two kidnapped Kosovo Albanians and one Serb who were accused of spying on the KLA. Two Serb policemen were killed in Prilep, south of Decani on the 20th of November. And the KLA was reportedly preparing fighting positions, building bunkers, and establishing their own check-points to harass Serbs. Are you familiar with any of that at all?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no information about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right. This is a daily report on the 14th of November. "The KLA responded aggressively to a scheduled police patrol on the Malisevo-Blace road. The police showed great restraint when armed and uniformed KLA appeared on the patrol road." Are you familiar with that at all?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I am not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: The report goes on to say that, "The KLA had become increasingly active in the Malisevo area and KDOM receives reports of KLA retribution killings of Albanians suspected of collaboration with the Serbs. The police claim that the KLA killed an ethnic Albanian police officer and abducted his son in Prekoluka in Decani municipality." Do you think anything about that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Then November --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: For this -- the incident that was just talked about, we don't have a date. I don't know if we should maybe have a date, if there is one, for this particular last incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It says it's the daily report for the 14th of November, and it's just a continuation of the previous question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Sorry. My misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: 20th of November, 1998, "The KLA ambushed a commercial vehicle used by the police in Prilep south of Decani. Two policemen killed, three wounded. A KLA commander in the area noted that the KLA central command had ordered KLA soldiers to observe the cease-fire; however, the commander said that he could not control all of his patrols all of the time." Are you familiar with that at all?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: By the 20th of November, were you the Chief of Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not at that time. I was not yet appointed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think that's the problem, Mr. Ackerman, with these questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It may be, Your Honour, but there are some questions that arise out of them in any event I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: This report goes on to say this: "KLA patrols in the area often encounter Serbian patrols, and under KLA rules of engagement, are allowed to fire." Now, were those the rules of engagement that were in effect when you were there with the KLA?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what it was like for that period. I already pointed out yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: No. I'm asking you what the rules of engagement were like when you were active with the KLA in Kosovo. Did the rules of engagement permit KLA patrols to open fire on Serbian patrols on sight? When they'd see them, they could open fire on them. Was that rules of engagement in effect when you were there?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Do you know when that changed?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: After I took over my duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now, this commander who said that he couldn't control all of his patrols all the time, I take it that that's a problem that all commanders have to deal with; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: This is some information that apparently comes from the United Kingdom, and it tells us that on the 16th of March in 1999, there was little evidence of a cease-fire in Kosovo. Clashes continued on 15 March to the west of Vucitrn. The VJ said that nine soldiers were wounded in an attack by the UCK in Podujevo between Decani and Djakovica. Are you familiar with this attack, the 15th of March on the VJ vehicles?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Could you have ordered that attack?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: This report continues: "The UCK attacked VJ vehicles in several places along the road between Pristina and Podujevo on 14 and 15 March." Are you familiar with this attack and did you order this attack?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This attack was not ordered by me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: The report goes on to talk about an incident in October of 1998 when five VJ soldiers were killed by a KLA ambush on 30 September, actually. The KLA soldiers were positioned on both sides of the border and subsequently all of them retreated into Albania. Now, I suspect you don't know anything about this either, but was this a common tactic by the KLA to go back and forth across that border. They would cross over and attack the VJ, and then cross back into Albania where they were safe. Did that go on with some frequency?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And then the final sentence of that particular report says: "There was no fighting," and this -- we're talking about September/October of 1998. "There was no fighting except in response to KLA attacks." Do you agree with that, the information we have from the United Kingdom?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that period. Maybe it is as it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. I want you to look at a document. It's Exhibit 4D32. Now, this appears to be a letter addressed to Wesley Clark, the commander of the NATO forces. And I'd like you to look first at the very last page, at the bottom of the very last page of that document, please. There.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Could you kind of zero in on the seal and the signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Is that seal familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the seal is familiar, but the signature is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right. Now, in this document, it's purported to be a letter from the KLA General Staff apparently to General Clark. And one of the things it talks about on the 18th of April, 1999, is that, in the third paragraph: "NATO aviation masters completely the air." Do you know that to be true, that there was total air superiority by NATO or air command by NATO by April of 1992 -- of 1999?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And you'll notice on basically the last page of that document there's a paragraph where it speaks of that again. "We think the time has come to be rushed with utmost urgency in the first variant option. We know that your aviation acted with the maximum do not deal with the bees, but with their nest, but to Serbia except for their aviation whose nest you have completely destroyed, the other nests," it says what they are, "are dispersed," tanks and things of that nature. So this indicates that Serb aviation was completely destroyed by this time; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. It's not me who has written this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, forget about the document. You were a commander in the field at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We can read it as easily as he can, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Isn't it the case that NATO had basically taken out all of the possibility for Serbian aviation to function by April of 1999?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that because it was a time when I was handing over my duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, you weren't being attacked by any Serbian aviation, were you?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have no information about that. During the time I was here, I have no information about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Tell me what kind of contacts the KLA had with the US military and in what ways was the US -- United States military assisting the KLA.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already explained to you that during my duty I had no contacts whatsoever with other armies.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Did you hear about any contacts between members of the KLA and members of the United States military and any assistance coming from the United States military to KLA?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'd like you to look at a document, Exhibit 4D33, just to see if you have any explanation for what appears in it. This is a document from the Austrian embassy in Belgrade, and it is a report apparently on a meeting that Jan Kickert, and I think maybe someone else, had with representatives from the United States and the Russian Federation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And if we go down to one, two, three, four, the fourth bullet point.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: "On the other hand, by their own admission, there have been long contacts with UCK representatives at US military attache level." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not familiar with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Are you familiar with any contact between Holbrooke and the UCK, like in Junik?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in Junik I know that Mr. Holbrooke was there in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And had his picture taken with some KLA fighters? I assume you've seen that picture.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have seen that picture. It was taken in Junik village.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right. Do you know of a -- of a KLA commander by the name of Ylli, Y-l-l-i?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the name is not familiar.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know who Asllan Bushati is?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: How about a KLA commander with the nickname Remi, R-e-m-i, do you know him? He's supposed to be KLA commander for the operational subzone of Llap, L-l-a-p?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And do you agree that the position of the KLA was what he represents here: "There cannot be any agreement between the UCK and the Serbian forces, because in the final analysis, there is nothing for us to agree on within the borders of Kosovo. We can only agree on their full withdrawal from the Republic of Kosovo." True?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember this, but probably it is like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And he went on to say that: "The UCK has explicitly stated several times that it does not recognise the parliament and self-styled government of Kosovo and therefore conduct negotiations on or around Kosovo if the UCK is not involved in these talks." That was the position of the KLA, was it not?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right. Do you know who Shukri Buja is?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: He was a KLA commander, was he not?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was the commander of the operational zone of Nerodime.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Do you know about an occasion where he raped an Albanian woman, who was detained in a prison, that he had something to do with?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no information about that.
