utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Do you have any information about him beating a gypsy prisoner to death with a wooden stick at this place?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no knowledge about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Do you have knowledge about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman, the law of diminishing returns is now in play. These questions are clearly ones this witness has no personal knowledge of.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, so far.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Do you know about a KLA prison that was located at Lapusnik in Glogovac municipality?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right. This question comes from Exhibit 4D34?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Which I'll ask to be put on the monitor now. And unfortunately, I only have it in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And this is a report from OSCE-Kosovo Verification Mission of 26 February through 4 March 1999. And it speaks about the Djeneral Jankovic area. It says: "It would appear that over 100 KLA members crossed the border and combined with the sub-militia, while encouraging the locals to leave. The incentive to move into this region is unclear, although a number of possibilities exist. By encouraging the movements of IDPs," internally displaced persons, "the international media was able to claim a Serb offensive was underway. Indeed, the EuroNews reported that a Serb offensive took place, which combined with pictures of Serb vehicles on the move and innocent villagers looking pathetic, was a coup for the ethnic Albanian cause. The Koha Ditore described the village of Kacanik as being a 'ghost town,' which verifiers noted was untrue and initial reports from the region had somehow suggested a massacre had taken place." Now, this seems to suggest what was going on there. And that Djeneral Jankovic area was some sort of a big propaganda ploy by the KLA to generate sympathy from the outside, and that happened on more than one occasion, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no information about the case you are quoting.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: But I asked you if that kind of activity was a tactic of the KLA, to try to engender foreign sympathy and support and to bring NATO into the war.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: The top of the next page under the heading "Elsewhere." It reads that: "The KLA force in Podujevo area managed to carry out an attack in the town itself, effectively taking the fight to the Serbs, as opposed to simply reacting and defending, as had been claimed in the past." Are you familiar with that attack?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No order was given to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: If we go to the top of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, there are two separate issues there. No order was given to that effect is one thing, but the question was: Were you aware of this taking place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Did the OSCE not have regular contact with your General Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The OSCE had contacts with the General Staff, with the political directorate that was responsible for maintaining such contacts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So your attention was not drawn to breaches of the cease-fire, such as the one that's set out on this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To my recollection, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, that's a matter of great concern if the observers weren't drawing to your attention that the cease-fire was being breached. Are you sure that that was the position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am saying that I had no information about that. Maybe the group that maintained contact with the OSCE had such information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: If we go to the top of the next page, the first full paragraph says -- speaks about VJ forces within Kosovo and their increased training. It says about the VJ forces that their actions have been somewhat low-key, in light of what can only be described as KLA provocations.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now, you know, don't you, that KLA was doing everything it could to provoke the Serb forces, the VJ, the police, into attacking them so that they could try to get NATO involved in this fight. Now, you know that was happening because that was a tactic of the army that you were a commander of, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time I was Chief of Staff. With respect to these cases, it was not the tactic of the KLA to provoke the Serbian forces in order for the NATO to intervene.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Why would the OSCE report this in an official report? Look, for instance, at their assessment over on page 5 near the bottom of the page under the words "Assessment." We'll see if what it says there is this: "In recognising the power of the media, the ethnic Albanians will continue to work on international sympathy for their cause. The plight of the internally displaced persons remains their strongest weapon, and therefore other incidents involving the movement of large numbers of people can be expected. Careful examination of each scenario needs to take place, and one is no longer able to make the assumption that internally displaced people indicate a Serb attack will take place." Now, I can't imagine why OSCE would make a report with that language if -- if what I suggested wasn't going on. Don't you agree?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not saying that the OSCE report has not given the right assessment. They must have based this assessment on something, but to your question, whether it was the KLA tactics to provoke the Serb forces, my answer is no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, let's look then at the last section of this report, which is headed "The Next Week."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: How is that going to help us, Mr. Ackerman? You've got clear answers from the witness. He's conceding that the OSCE has got it right, but as far as he's concerned, it wasn't a specific tactic. Now, are we going to advance our knowledge anymore with this?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Oh, all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I know exactly what you're thinking. You're thinking we can read this and it makes no sense for you to read it to us, but this is a public trial and the public doesn't have this document, they can't read it, and I think the public is entitled to know the evidence in this case, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: If the public wish any public document in this case, they have access to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, it's very difficult for someone sitting in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: A public trial is not a trial in which every piece of material is scrutinised in open court. A public trial is a trial which takes place in public and is open to public scrutiny. These are two entirely different concepts. It's not -- it's just not feasible to present every last piece of material in any trial of this nature on TV and live TV for everyone to watch as they consume their leisure time in whatever part of the world they live. That's not what a public trial means.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, I totally agree with that, Your Honour, and I certainly wasn't suggesting that I should stand here and read every exhibit so the public can hear me read it, but the pertinent parts of some of these documents, I think, absolutely need to be part of the public record in this case. And I know that there are people out there watching us right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: At this -- in this last section, "The Next Week," I just want to draw to your attention some things said by the OSCE: "The international community can comprehend pictures of VJ tanks and easily label them as aggressive Serb activities. The KLA will seek to exploit this and will therefore provoke the Serbs over the coming week." In the final paragraph: "If the KLA continue to ambush the MUP, the FRY security forces will be compelled to respond." So what they're saying here is that KLA [Realtime transcript read in error "OSCE"] is propagandising what's going on and violating the cease-fire to try to provoke the Serbs into some kind of action. Isn't that true and isn't that what was happening?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already stated that the aim of the KLA, while I was the Chief of General Staff, was not to provoke the Serb forces in order to make NATO forces intervene. As I said, I'm not questioning the assessment of the OSCE reports because they have to be based on something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think line 18 there of page 50 must be reference to the KLA rather than the OSCE. And that's certainly how the witness understood the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes, I think it's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I think I have just one other matter that I want to go into with you. At least your initial time -- at least your initial time in Kosovo was spent in the area of Haradinaj's command, and I take it you got to know Haradinaj reasonably well?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the time I used to know him, I can for some part of it say yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the term that was used by he and members of his command, issuing papers for Drenica?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Do you know anything about the killings of a couple of people named Uki Reshapi [phoen] and Nezli Alilaj [phoen] by Haradinaj or his assistants who were issued papers for Drenica?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have no knowledge about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right. My last question then is: Are you familiar with a KLA organisation called the Black Eagles?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And this was a KLA unit that wore black uniforms and was led by a person named Idriz Balaj?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And I take it you know that in July or August of 1998 Idriz Balaj was accused of raping an Albanian woman who was accused of collaborating with the Serbs. Are you familiar with that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not. This is another period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And you didn't hear about that when you went to Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: If it's the case that Idriz Balaj basically admitted that and said that he'd been ordered to do it, was he still in that position later, after you arrived there? Was he still the commander of this Black Eagles organisation?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I visited there, I was not in the position of the Chief of Staff, and for this particular case, I was not informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure that you answered my question. Was he still the commander of the Black Eagles when you arrived in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I went there for the first time to visit Dukagjin area, I know that he was commander of this unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, just for the record and the good-faith basis for that last series of Haradinaj and Balaj questions, they come from the OTP's indictment of Mr. Haradinaj. And with that, that's all I have. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. We shall go briefly into private session to protect the position of an individual in the interests of justice.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in public session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: I have a question for you, please. You -- you gave a picture of the organisation as it worked, the KLA. Now, it must be having some -- some sort of a system of intelligence, whereby reports from the lower echelons or areas would come up to a person like yourself when you were the Chief of Staff. Now, to -- while answering questions from the learned counsel very recently, you've just given a bold denial, which of course means that those reports would not contain all that or you did not consult it or were there no reports and all what was being talked of was something which never happened or was there a suppression of facts. What happened, because in an organisation, there is always a reporting. The higher officers learn of things, they learn of the activities of their junior officers, they find out what their activities are. They write their reports, they recommend them, they place them here, and they are in different positions. But from your statement it appears that either there was no nexus or there was no reporting or there was no intelligence. Would you be kind enough in letting us know about how the intelligence worked and how the reporting system was established within the KLA, please. I'm thankful.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I've mentioned it earlier, during the previous days - and I'm speaking for the period while I was Chief of Staff - the commanders would come directly to report to the staff. And I've mentioned before that in March we met with zone commanders. And whatever they reported to me was what I knew, and for -- from what they have reported, I don't remember that I have been informed about this. As for 1998, I was not in that position and there was no way I could know about the reporting from different zones. I'm only speaking of what I know based on the reports I received from zone commanders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: But what was suggested by the learned counsel regarding some of the facts related and pertained to your tenure as the Chief of Staff, on that also, there was a reply of unawareness on your part. But you haven't replied to my question which basically was: Was there an intelligence service within the KLA, being such a big organisation? And secondly, was there a system of verification of reports if somebody gave you a correct report or not a correct report and was there cross-checking because that's the way the intelligence works? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Within the frames of the staff, there was the directorate of intelligence and counter-intelligence. There were at lower levels as well, in the level of brigade. I'm speaking of the reports that I've received, and since a long time has passed, I can't possibly remember all the reports. It is possible that such cases might have happened, but for the moment, I cannot answer by simply yes or no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: To whom did the director of intelligence report and how was the report passed? Did it go through you as the Chief of Staff or was it sent separately, without your knowledge? Whom did he report to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] During January, February, and March, reports were made and -- including reports to the commander of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: And these did not pass through you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not all of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: This is a vague answer. What type of reports passed through you? You were the Chief of Staff.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] During that period, I mean January, February, and March, the reports of the intelligence directorate were mainly on the movements of the Serb forces, their positions, and their state of readiness, while -- I'm speaking about reports that I've received from them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: Thank you -- oh, I mean, we're still not getting it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Zyrapi. My name is Djuro Cepic. I'm one of the Defence lawyers, and I will be asking you a couple of questions. First of all, I would like to talk about the training areas in Albania, where for a time you yourself trained members of the so-called KLA. Can you please tell me whether you know if there were any foreign instructors there who trained the so-called KLA.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During January, February, March the training was conducted by me and other fellow officers, former JNA officers. We didn't have any other instructors.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Are you referring now to Albania or to Kosmat?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm referring to Albania; that's what your question was.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now that we're talking about Albania, can you please tell me where the training areas and centres for the KLA fighters were located.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm speaking about the time when I was there. The training was carried out in mountainous areas. There was a training facility in the mountains of Dajti outside Tirana. I was there and contacted the training of these soldiers. I don't know for other areas where training was carried out, and I'm speaking about March, April, and May --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You're now talking about March, April, and May. You started answering during January, February, and March the training was conducted by me and other fellow officers. And you're referring there to 1998, I think. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, 1998.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And now you make the point March, April, and May. Now, when did you first arrive and become involved in training?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I arrived there in Tirana sometime in mid-March 1998 and I stayed there until May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Would it perhaps refresh your memory if I were to say that one of the training areas was in Tropoja in the village of Isidol and then in the village of Babin near Bajram Curija and then in the village of Heljsan on the Tropoja-Kuks road. Where the fighters were massing up for their infiltration into the Kosova territory, then in the village of Kruma, the village of Vlahnja, Peskopeja, the port of Drac. Let me now not enumerate any further, but would that perhaps refresh your memory?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the locations that you mentioned Tropoja, Krum, these were indeed training locations after the bombing started in 1999, April/May of this year. To my knowledge, Durres, at that time, was not a location suitable for training because it's a town. Maybe it was as a base where Albanians from different parts of Europe were arriving to join.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And would it not be correct to say -- precisely, yes, precisely. And would it not be correct to say that for the purposes of the so-called KLA, the depots, garages, army barracks, that they were put to the use of the so-called KLA, so would that be correct to say?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you are referring to is about the period April, May, June 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about 1998.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I already said, in 1998 I already told you the locations where I was and where I conducted the training. I don't think I've mentioned depots or garages or other facilities of the Albanian army. There was certain private houses used as collection points for weapons, but during my time, I don't know of any other locations except for those that I've already mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, I make this claim on the basis of excerpts by -- from a book "Story About Freedom and War" by Ramush Haradinaj, which is mentioned in page 4, paragraph 1 of your 2005 statement. In page 15 of the transcript today, you stated that the future fighters would come from all over Europe. Can you tell us whether there were any fighters originating from Bosnia and Herzegovina that joined the ranks of the so-called KLA?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Albanians who lived there, yes, to my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We saw an exhibit here marked P2464 that you brought before the Court here, and it pertains to disciplinary measures imposed on soldier Hasim Beja and it is stated there that he was from Bosnia. And this is stated as a reason why this disciplinary measure was actually drafted in the Bosnian language rather than in Albanian. So he was not an Albanian, right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my knowledge, he is from Kosova, Bosnian from Kosova, and they speak Serbian, and I even mentioned the village where, Kalluder is the name, where the population is Bosnian and they speak Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the registrar to prepare 3D177 for use.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: In the meantime, Mr. Zyrapi, did you know that there was some fighters from Saudi Arabia as well as from Ireland and there was an attempt for some soldiers to arrive from as far as the Philippines? Did you know about that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There haven't been such soldiers in Kosova. As far as the Albanians are concerned, they came from all over the world, even from beyond the Atlantic, from the United States, from Australia, and other countries. This is what I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, did you hear of Ekrem Avdija born in 1971 in Kosovska Mitrovica? He was a KLA fighter.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't seem to remember this name. I can't possibly remember all the names of the KLA soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, I wanted to put his assertion to you, that being that in the village of Donje Prekaze in Srbica, he himself established a military camp for the training of Mujahedin. The name was Abu Bekir Sidik and the name of the company was the Mujahedin Company in Kosovo, the Drenica Company. Did you know about that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which period are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: June 1998.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no knowledge about that, what you are putting to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Another question on the topic. Did you know of an attempt with some other KLA fighters in the same period of time, or rather, there was a group of the Mujahedin from Saudi Arabia who were supposed to be transferred to Smonica in mid-June. There were four citizens of Saudi Arabia. There was an Irish person using the pseudonym of Abu Omer, two unknown persons, two Arab persons, and another person who was a citizen of Malaysia by the name of Abu Hamet. In that incident, a skirmish ensued involving them and the security forces, whereupon two people were wounded. Did you know about that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I think the witness has already said that he did not know of any Mujahedin and they are just repeating the question in another form I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And it relates to a time for which there is no basis in the evidence to suppose that he would have knowledge of these matters. Let's get to something that the witness is likely to be able to deal with, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I suppose you don't know about the north of Albania where during 1998 there was a Bin Ladin's cell there. I suppose you don't know about that either?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, the boogeymen are not likely to advance the progress of this case, Mr. Cepic. Let's concentrate on real live issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I believe we will deal with it during the Defence case, and I have a basis for this question. And I surely hope I will be in a position to explain it to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You've described your arrival in Kosovo. You said you came on the 28th of May, 1998. You entered illegally, of course, same as on many other occasions where you moved between Kosovo and Albania. Can you tell us which routes were used by the fighters to enter Kosovo from Albania, and what were the roads used for supply for the KLA? If this may be of assistance, perhaps we could see P2469.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the court administration for assistance so that the witness could indicate the routes used.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a very small map to accurately describe the routes used. We used many routes whenever we could have access to Kosova, both soldiers and material means.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Would it not be easier for the witness just to tell us the routes that were used? These diagrams often don't really assist us very precisely. Why don't you just tell us your knowledge of the routes that fighters used to come into Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is rather difficult for me indeed to give you accurate information, but when I personally entered, I entered from Vllana, passing through the Kurore mountain. I descended to Demjan village, then continued my way through Drenoc village and then I entered Drenice. The supplies came from other passages, but I cannot give you accurate information because it is difficult to draw the lines of these passages. I just described one route that I myself used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But are there not other names of places through which the routes run that you can give us which will give counsel an indication of where this was taking place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I indicated the places I travelled from, that is one route for people and for materiel means, and this was used also by others. They use also the Gjakova route, which we have described earlier from Tropoja, Bajram Curija and Zal Her. And then there was another route from Koretice but I cannot describe accurately every possible place, but these are the places which the -- from which the border was crossed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Would you still like something drawn, Mr. Cepic?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: No. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe it is far simpler to pursue this line of questioning or this mode.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what routes were used to supply the central and the northern area of the KLA? For example, if there was a supply of weapons and a number of soldiers who were going towards Drenica and further up, where would they go if they went through Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the direction of Gjakova, from the border you passed through Gllogjan territory and then followed the road to the villages in the territory of Kline, Mrasor, then towards Malisheve, and then in the direction of Drenice. That was the route we used for that purpose. We used many other routes as well, but this was the most frequently used route.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: How about the units of the KLA in the east and the south-east in the municipality of Kacanik, which routes were used for their supply?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The routes were those coming from the Macedonian border.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Cepic, we'll be breaking in a moment. If the point here is that there are areas where action by the army or the police is justified, there's no reason why you can't put specific routes to the witness and obtain confirmation of the ones that really matter for the case, if that is in fact what the aim of this cross-examination is. Are we likely to finish the witness today, do you know?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It will depend on Mr. Lukic, but as far as I'm concerned, I will do my utmost, and this should be half an hour tops, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, can you help me?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can help you. I don't know whether you would be satisfied with my answer, but I think that I would be left only with half an hour. I don't think I can finish my cross in half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, we'll -- if this is convenient, we'll be sitting until ten past 7.00 anyway, since we started late. So what we'll do is stop at 7.00 and hear argument about the evidence that -- to which there's objection taken from the next scheduled witness, and that will allow us to make clear how that evidence is going to be presented. It's been hanging there as an issue to be dealt with. Now, if Mr. O'Sullivan has been given the wrong impression and is inconvenienced by that, then we'll change the arrangement. But if it suits him, then we could do that at 7.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I believe Mr. O'Sullivan will be in the courtroom at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, with that in mind, may I have the next witness released to go back to his hotel?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sounds like it, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, can I just raise the one issue that is kind of sitting out there as an unknown. We've got a 186-page transcript of a statement from this witness that was just provided to us, and that could cause some additional cross-examination in the morning and it may not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, you'll just need to put that novel aside tonight, Mr. Ackerman, and read something much more gripping.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It would be so nice if I could do that. You have no idea how much I have -- the last word I wanted to hear was there was this transcript; I'm telling you that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Anyway, I take the point you make and I'm grateful for the fact that you're addressing the issue so expeditiously. Mr. Zyrapi, we need our break again. Could you leave with the usher, and we'll back in half an hour, at 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, so as to conclude with the topic of routes, is it correct that one of the marked routes was the one going across the Junik mountains, through the Junik village, as well as Decani, Caragoj, Jablanica, and further on toward Drenica?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is one of the routes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Another important route went via Mount Pastrik, Prizren, river Drin, the village of Zerze, Orahovac, and further onwards. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the Pashtrik route was one of the routes that we used, and I mentioned in this context, the route that I used.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Since we are on the topic of Mount Junik, there is also the location of Kosare there. That was a border point of the VJ at the time. After the conflict in Kosovo, you provided -- you gave an interview to journalist Harim Gazi. And in that interview you mentioned that one of the most important battles including the KLA was in the region of Kosare?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Did you participate in the planning and organising of a military action called Strela Jedan, arrow 1, which commenced on the 9th of April, 1999, and was directed towards the area of Kosare?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did participate in the planning and organising of Shigjeta, while for April the plan was drafted by the command of this unit. That was in Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me who commanded that unit?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of this unit was Rrustem Berisha.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Was Rrustem Berisha the officer of the Albanian army or a KLA officer?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rrustem Berisha was a former JNA officer and a KLA officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You know that the operation commenced on the 9th of April, 1998 [as interpreted], on the Serb Christmas --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Easter.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can you please just utter a spoken answer for the transcript?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Apologies. Just one correction for the transcript. I said "Easter," not "Christmas." Thank you. I also said "1999" not "1998."

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Zyrapi, is that correct that Strela Jedan commenced on the 9th of April, 1999, on the Serbian Easter and that there was some heavy combat?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: In one of the answers the expression "Shideta" was used. Is that the same operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Shigjeta. It was the name of the operation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Not Strela Jedan?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note, Shigjeta has the same meaning in Albanian as the Strela in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thank the booths for the clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, speaking from the military point of view, since you participated in the planning of the operation, why was it important for the KLA?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Speaking about the operation in general, it was important because during that time the procurement of weapons for the KLA was very weak. It was very difficult for us to procure weapons, and then as a result of the beginning of NATO bombing, it was very important for us to open up corridors for procuring weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: This action lasted until mid-May. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: In early May, in the area of Mount Pastrik, Strela Dva, Arrow 2, commenced. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's when the operation started in Pastrik zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: It had the same goal as Strela Jedan?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zyrapi. Let's not waste any more time on that. You mentioned quite a number of things about the KLA structure, the zones, the brigades, and other units. But I'm interested in the following. In the statement you gave in 2005, when describing the unit commanded by Daut Haradinaj, you said that in addition to two battalions it also comprised 21 village staffs. I'm interested in these village staffs in the territory of the entire Kosovo. Isn't it correct that such staffs comprised mainly the inhabitants of the particular villages?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've mentioned it in my statement, the local staffs refer to the villages where they were formed or to the municipalities where they were formed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I wanted to know about the composition of those local staffs. Did they mainly include the local inhabitants, the local villagers?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: The KLA armed those, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I took up duty, these staffs were already formed and they were supplied by the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Is it correct if I say that, due to the shortage of uniforms, most of such staff members wore civilian clothes, although they had been distributed weapons?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During that period, the local staffs did not have that many uniforms. They had a few only.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, are these personnel in addition to the 17 or 18.000 that you described as the complement of the KLA armed forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. These were for the earlier periods of time, from March and on, when the re-organisation started.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, if you can clarify this, I'd be grateful, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will endeavour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, as best you can remember, when were the local staffs established?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know when each and every local staff was established, but when I took up duty, the majority of local staffs had already been formed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me how much of the Kosovo territory they covered? Did it include most of the villages in Kosovo? Can you give us a percentage? Say out of a total number of villages, how many of them had their local staffs?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is difficult for me to give you a percentage. I cannot tell you precisely how many, in percentage, they represented of the entire territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: May we conclude that that percentage was quite high?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I arrived, a certain percentage existed but not very high. Those areas that I visited, they had local staffs, but I cannot give you an accurate percentage.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zyrapi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I would still like the question I asked answered. You gave us evidence that when you were Chief of Staff, the KLA had 17 to 18.000 soldiers in Kosovo. Does that include the people who were members of the local village staffs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] During that period of time, no, because the local staffs then no longer existed, but there were units and brigades, as I've already explained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But you've just told us that these local staffs existed when you took over.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The local staffs existed when I entered Kosova, and then the re-organisation took place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So what happened to the local staffs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were included in frames of the units, then later the platoons, the squads, the brigades were formed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So a platoon or a squad might simply be made up of the members of the KLA from a particular village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, there were such cases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Were they in a way - I'm now referring to the local staffs - still in the overall KLA system in the sense that they were subordinate to certain units, depending on their actual location?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I entered Kosova, some of them were subordinated to the zone commands; but later on, they were re-organised. I'm speaking about the period of time June/July. Some were under the zones and some were still under development. At that time, there were no formed units such as brigades or battalions.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zyrapi. When you spoke about the number of troops, I would like to investigate this issue by asking you one question. Do you know a gentleman by the name of Pleurat Sediu who was in the KLA staff in Tirana in the spring of 1999?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anyone by the name of Pleurat Sediu, at least this is how the name was interpreted to me. I don't know anyone by that name.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Let me spell the name and that should clarify perhaps this issue. So the name is P-l-e-u-r-a-t, Pleurat, and the last name is Sediu, S-e-d-i-u.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pleurat Sediu, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: What was his function at the time?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my knowledge, he was the spokesperson of the KLA outside Kosova.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, he gave an interview to Laura Rozen, published on the 24th of May, 1999, in which he says, I quote: "We have 35.000 soldiers, KLA soldiers, in there, women and men of military age, armed, and engaged in combat." Do you agree with what he says that in May 1999 the KLA had 35.000 soldiers?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the information that I had, until March there was 17.000 to 18.000 that I mentioned. I don't know if there were 35.000 engaged in the KLA by May. I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like Defence Exhibit 5D20 to be brought to screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You can see the underlined section here, the relevant section that I quoted to you. So this is paragraph 3. Can we now move on to the second page, paragraph 3. Mr. Zyrapi -- so he claims that there were 35.000 fighters. Did you perhaps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. -- Yes, Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I think that very statement by -- from the article that has just been put to the witness, the witness said he didn't think that number was correct, but he didn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Indeed, he has.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, we will now move on to another topic. This is the topic of weapons. You said to us that the so-called KLA had had only light infantry weapons, rifles, AK-47 that comprised 70 to 80 per cent of the weapons, light machine-guns, heavy machine-guns, just a few mortars. My learned colleague Mr. Ackerman asked you about some other weapons. Now, my question to you is whether you had any heavy artillery, whether the KLA had any heavy artillery?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've mentioned earlier, inside Kosova these were the weapons that were used. We did not have heavy artillery weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like the Defence Exhibit 5D19 to be brought to screen. This is a video-clip that lasts only about. This is a video-clip that lasts only about 40 seconds, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, can you please describe this artillery piece here. Do you perhaps -- can you perhaps identify it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first that we saw were recoilless cannons. I said earlier that there were no heavy artillery weapons inside Kosova. What we saw in the second part of the clip, it's a heavy artillery weapon but it is not inside the territory of Kosova.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me where was it then?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is outside the Kosova border. It's in the territory of Albania, but I don't know exactly in which location.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: So how do you know that it was not in Kosovo but in Albania when you don't know its exact location?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Simply because we did not have heavy artillery weapons inside Kosova, and this is from the period May/June 1999 when this heavy artillery weapon was there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Let's ask the question the other way around. How do you know that that was in Albania?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the appearance of the soldiers that I saw, they were outside of Kosova and that artillery is outside Kosova. The person speaking on the clip, he was not in Kosova, he was outside.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So these were KLA soldiers; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And you know -- or you say that they were normally outside, but how does that prove that this particular film was taken outside of Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can tell that this clip was made outside Kosova because of the way the soldiers look and because of the fact that we did not have heavy artillery weapons in Kosova. And this event took place during the Shigjeta operation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What do you mean by the way the soldiers look?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Their clothes, and the fact that in Kosova we did not have helmets; and, as I said, we did not have heavy artillery weapons inside Kosova.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Cepic, are you -- have you a foundation for saying that that was in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that the witness gave us the correct information, and now he specified the time, the relevant time-period. He said that this was the Strela operation, the operation mounted by the KLA into Kosovo from the Albanian side and this artillery fire was in fact the artillery support for other KLA units engaged in the Kosare and Pastrik sectors.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Is that correct, Mr. Zyrapi?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And the artillery fire targeted mostly the Caragoj valley area. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not -- I am not familiar with the term Caragoj valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: That's an area beyond the state border, the border between Kosova and Albania, in the direction of Djakovica. The villages of Meja, Korenica, Junik.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in that direction, that's where the Serb forces were.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zyrapi, in your statement you described how in July 1998 you were in the village of Jablanica in the KLA staff and that Ramush Haradinaj escorted you around and showed you the territory around the Glodjan village and the other villages in that sector near the Radonjic lake. Do you know that when the Serb forces returned to those positions in early September, that some bodies were found there, bodies of civilians, Serbs, Albanians who were not loyal to the KLA. Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did visit the area at that time, but I had no information about these cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And do you know that in the village of Jablanica, precisely at the time when you were in the staff, that a detention centre was located in that compound and that 12 people went missing from that detention facility? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. During the time I visited the positions and the units in that area, I didn't come across such a detention facility.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Just one more question in this line of questioning so as not to waste our precious time. You said that your staff was located -- your headquarters was located at the Berisa mountains. The village of Klecka lies to the north of this area. Do you know that crematorium, a lime kiln, was located there where more than 25 civilians had been burned and KFOR, in fact, drafted the statement some remains, human remains, were found there. Do you know anything about that? And two brothers, the Murzaku brothers were arrested subsequently?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the staff was positioned in Berisa mountains, it was during the time when I became Chief of Staff in November, but I had no knowledge that this existed there at that time. It is a part engaged in the production of limestone there, but I have not heard of this kind of use.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And to my last question. You brought to the Prosecution the interim regulations on the internal affairs in the army. This is Exhibit 2449. On page 3 of the English translation where the flag is discussed, Albanian version, first paragraph on page 4, it says, I quote: "Hatred for the eternal enemy which is destroying," text missing, "and endeavouring to take away everything sacred and fundamental to us." Mr. Zyrapi, who is the eternal enemy?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this statement it is -- it means the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thank you, Mr. Zyrapi.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cepic, for directing your questions so pointedly to significant issues. Now, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good evening, Mr. Zyrapi. The bad news is that I have questions for you, and the good news is that I'm the last Defence counsel to have questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like the Prosecution Exhibit 2447 to be brought to the screen because this might be of assistance, and I will, by way of introduction, say the following.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is a map on which you described what routes your forces used to pull out from the area A to the area B, area C. So we're talking about the Serb offensive in late March 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please zoom in a little bit so that we can see those areas A, B, and C, and D. Just a little bit more and just a little bit more. Thank you. That would be fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The main force pulled out from one area to another; that's one thing. But do you know that some units tried to break through the encirclement, that they tried to break through towards the east, the Trnje area, and that there was fighting there, too.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which period are you talking about and Trnje village?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about when the units retreated from area A to area B.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the units withdrew from zone A to B, from the reports and information that we received, retreated to zone B. And I have no information about any other movement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So you have no information about any units trying to retreat towards Albania and that there was fighting in Landovica, too, in Petrovo Selo, even in Zur. Although there had been no KLA forces in Landovica before that period, fighting was recorded in this period in that village. Landovica is to the south of Mala Krusa, for instance, Pirane.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We talked about the period when the units withdrew to zone B, and I have no information that any units went in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If you don't know, it's a legitimate answer. I was just trying to verify something. You say that in the encirclement there were some brigades, and you specified which ones. May we conclude that not all of the KLA brigades were inside the encirclement and that some were outside?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we talked about the zones, A, B, C, the units and the brigades found in those zones of responsibility, 24, 25, they were within those zones. I'm talking about that period and those moments. The numbers were 124 and 125 of the brigades.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How about some other brigades, 111th, 112th, and 113? Or, say, 162nd, the one we mentioned the other day, were they all in the encirclement or not?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Brigades 111, 112, 113, 114, they were in the context of zone A, whereas 162 was in zone B -- D. Not B but D.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How many KLA brigades were outside the encirclement, do you know?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No brigades were outside the zones that I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, was the evidence not here of a withdrawal from A through B to the line at C?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, but I'm trying to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, no, just bear with me. I'm not challenging anything at the moment. Was that the evidence originally?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: From which it would follow that the 111th to 114th would have to withdraw as well. Can we clarify where they went to when this happened?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'll try to ask the witness to clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Zyrapi, you heard what the Honourable Judges would like to hear about. What about the brigades that Judge Bonomy mentioned, did they retreat from zone A to B and then to C?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I talk about zones A, B, and D, I mean the Brigades 124, 123, and 125, but the other brigade was in the Drenica zone. It is zone E.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That makes sense now. It didn't make sense that these four brigades were being referred to as in A. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Beyond the zones which were in the encirclement, were there any armed KLA units?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my knowledge, all the units were within the territories that I described.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: For example, we have the following piece of data. Close to area A, we know that a junction was held by the KLA there and as well as the railroad in the town of Zerze and Bela Crkva and Celina, but this is not encompassed by the encirclement you drew on the map. Therefore, I'd like to know which units could have been in those villages. Were those some local units or parts of the brigades?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In those villages that you mentioned, there were no units of the KLA. All the units were within the lines that I described.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about the brigades from the Dukagjini area, were they also within the encirclement?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I spoke about the Pashtrik zone. The Dukagjin zone is in its own area with its own brigades.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I may have been insufficiently clear in my question. I wanted to know this: Outside of the territories you marked as those being encircled, were there any other KLA brigades there? We are not talking only about the Pastrik zone, but generally, about the KLA.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the reports I had, all the units were within the areas that I mentioned. There were no units outside these areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Perhaps you're tired and perhaps I am, too. But perhaps we could go back to the brigades which fell within the Dukagjini area. They were not encircled. Isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were in the territory where they were concentrated. But I describe the areas I had information on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps we could scroll down -- [In English] Sorry, we should scroll up. That's okay. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To the left we see the front line going through Izbica. Do you know what unit was in that village at that time?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Izbice, there was the units which fell within the responsibility of Brigade 112. It was part of its zone of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Your positions that were in the areas you marked as A, B, and C and primarily in zone A, had been fortified. There were embankments, trenches, and so on and so forth. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The lines I drew in zone A, area A, were the fortified front lines as much as we could to fortify them, and the units were stationed in those -- in that front line that I have described there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the same area of Retimlje, there was a make-shift hospital which could serve as many as 500 wounded troops at a time. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Reti there was a clinic. I think I mentioned it before.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In some villages, even before the outbreak of the conflict, there were or there had been no civilians. For example, the villages of Opterusa, Retimlje and Studencane [Realtime transcript read in error "Studimlje"]; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Even before the outbreak of the conflict, precisely because there was a possibility of one, the KLA had removed the civilian population from the villages of Opterusa, Retimlje, and Studencane [Realtime transcript read in error "Studimlje"]. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which period are you talking about, the beginning of the conflict in March?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, the very beginning of the conflict?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think your reference was to the village of Studencane and not to the village of Studimlje, as it now appears.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, Studencane.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, in the villages that were mentioned in the reports, there had been earlier artillery attacks and the population had been -- had left the villages before the attacks started.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. During the clashes, all the time there were NATO sorties. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You think during the combat the NATO forces were present where?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the air, NATO planes.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a time of air-strikes. Beginning from the 24th onwards there were constant bombings.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On that occasion, could you see them targeting Serbian positions and units?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there has been targeting of Serbian positions and units.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We received exhibit entitled "The Operational Zone of Drenica" from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have 6D107 put on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This Defence made an excerpt from this document. All I'd like to hear from you, provided you can still answer my questions this late in the day, is to confirm, or rather, to say whether these are the names of KLA commanders to the extent of your knowledge, of course. Although the document is in English, can you make out the names in the first column -- well, first of all, we see Adem Jashari at the top, then Selimi Sylejman, a.k.a. Sultan, and then we have the main HQ for the operational zone Drenica and this is the zone the document refers to. And then further down, we have four columns. The first one contains the name of municipality, then the unit in the second, the name in the third, and the position in the fourth, namely, the position of the given person. Can you recognise these names as the names of those people who belonged to the command structures of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please go to page 3 now, line 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We see here a name, Selimi Sylejman, a.k.a. Sultan, who was a KLA commander in the village of Ovcare at a certain point in time. Is this correct, and this of course was before he was promoted?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, he was commander in that village. Then he was promoted as zone commander, Drenica Operational Zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In column 3 it says Padalista as the village, and the village HQ commander is Loshi Liri. Do you know this KLA commander and did you ever meet him in Padalista?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't seem to remember the name. I've passed through many places, but I don't remember this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We will no longer be needing this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's time to break if it suits Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It would be a suitable time to break. Well, Mr. Zyrapi, we will have to interrupt your evidence again and resume it tomorrow. I assure you that at that time after he's had his rest, Mr. Lukic will be brief with you. You need to be back here tomorrow in the morning. We will resume at 9.00 tomorrow. Overnight, again, no discussion with anyone about your evidence. You may now leave the courtroom and we'll see you tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We shall now deal with the issues raised in a Defence motion to preclude the admission of Exhibit P2480, and an objection also in relation to the notice under Rule 65 ter of the testimony and exhibits to be used with the next witness. The submission, Mr. O'Sullivan, in relation to not admitting the exhibit P2480 in part or in whole is easy to follow. The position about the 65 ter notice is not quite so clear. It's become a bit clearer I think by the intimation of a notice to modify the 65 ter notice, which we'll take as an application for authority to do that. Is there really -- well, could you address that any further? Can you amplify that? Are you dissatisfied on that point still with the notice that the application that the Prosecution have made?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: We're aware of the notice, Your Honour, and our objection in this motion, I suppose, is in anticipation of any attempted modification of both the scope of examination and the exhibits which are broadened by that late notice, which came as late as last Thursday. The pre-trial brief of 10th of May set out both the scope of evidence, and annex C indicated the exhibits which would be tendered or used with this witness. It's on that basis we prepared for this witness. And there was no reason why this couldn't have been made known to us last May, when you ordered them to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Hannis, could you address that issue first of all.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you. With regard to the exhibits referred to in paragraph 9, I would indicate Exhibits P866, 867, and 1859 I do not intend to use. So we don't need to discuss those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, just give me a second until I get the motion here. This is -- and these are mentioned in paragraph 9. Give me these numbers again.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: 866, 867, and 1859, they're the last three in the running list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: As for the first one 2480. 2480 is the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We'll come back to that in a moment. If you could deal with the question of expanding the 65 ter notice first of all.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And tell me what justification there is for allowing you to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, there are two things I filed: The supplemental information from the 4th and 5th of November, which -- does Your Honour have that? This is where the defendant some corrections to his statement, about eight different corrections, and he told us -- I think we added four new paragraphs that basically go to his background.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I don't know if I have that. No, all I have readily to hand is a document which is an e-mail of the 11th of -- or the 7th --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The e-mail of the 7th of November.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And we listed seven items, basically, which are from the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I added those and requested leave to lead evidence about those in anticipation of the possibility that the Court did not allow in his statement. If his statement were allowed in, I was under the understanding that that evidence would be in. Whether I led it by asking the witness questions about it or not. But in light of the objection that was made about the statement not being permitted, then I thought I needed to raise that and seek permission to lead it in the event I have to present all of this witness's evidence via live testimony rather than a statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: When was the statement disclosed?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'll check with my case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That must have been before the trial started.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah. So the information was disclosed at that stage, albeit not made clear in the 65 ter summary as an issue. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour, as well as his transcript from his testimony in Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Go then to this second issue, which is the objection to the evidence being presented in writing in this way. The statement is P2480, is it, the witness's statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Um --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The principal --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, Rule 92 now and old Rule 89(F) will allow for the admissibility of this evidence in written form when the witness comes in and attests that the evidence contained therein is his declaration and he would answer the questions the same. Mr. O'Sullivan's motion, in the first part, said, well, this is a different case because this witness has disavowed this statement during his prior testimony by saying, well, that was only a working draft and I was speaking in English, not my native tongue, so there are some problems with it. But, Your Honour, in the supplemental information and based on our proofing with him, he's now reviewed the statement, he's now read a B/C/S version of the statement, he's made some changes, and I fully anticipate that when he comes in, he will attest that it's true and accurate and that he would answer the questions the way they are in the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There are other objections which I think are, principally, that there's a great deal in it that's expression of opinion without a clear indication of the basis for that opinion or view.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And secondly, there's an awful lot of hearsay about crucial issues in the case where the actual basis for this hearsay is rather vague. And speaking for myself at the moment, I think I would be greatly assisted by a presentation of this witness's evidence live and focused, because there's also stuff in the -- certainly, the second part of the statement as I would categorise it, which isn't so important to this case as it may have been to the Milosevic trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I fully agree, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And looking at it broadly, the first 11 pages or so are probably unobjectionable as a written document -- in fact, on to maybe the beginning -- the very top of page 12 where he's giving evidence of his own -- from his own direct knowledge. But after that, it's very difficult to disentangle fact from opinion and also work out exactly the basis for the hearsay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I agree, Your Honour. It is certainly not the most eloquent statement that you will see in this case. But we believe that the hearsay portions that Mr. O'Sullivan objects about and that you have some concern about, I believe, Your Honours, with direct and cross-examination, we can help clarify many of those. I do not think they are so inextricably intertwined that they cannot be sorted out by counsel and the Court. In many or most of the cases where it's clear that it is hearsay, he does identify his specific sources by name, such as Mr. Mihajlovic or Mr. Mijatovic, Mr. Perisic. He can and will explain some of the more general terms regarding hearsay, where he says, my SDB sources. I think he will indicate that those are two specific individuals. And my western sources, I think he will be more specific about that. I agree -- but I would indicate that the lay opinion evidence is not inadmissible if it regards matters within common human experience and those -- the specific basis of those opinions underlying the conclusion articulated. Finally, Judge, I do agree with what you said about the last part of the statement and I have gone through and identified --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The last part, though, is about three-quarters of it. It's the bulk of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I would say that I have gone through -- you don't have -- I guess I gave to Defence counsel yesterday B/C/S and English versions with numbered paragraphs, 1 through 178. I have gone through and identified some 23 paragraphs that I would propose to remove entirely for some of the reasons that you and Mr. O'Sullivan expressed concerns about. And another five where I would remove the last sentence because they are in the nature of "in my view" or "in my opinion" I think this, and there's no further explanation of the basis for that view or that opinion. However, I think the rest of it is appropriate for you to consider as written evidence. And with that statement and my efforts to clarify some of the other things, I think that's the most efficient way to present the bulk of his evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Are you going to give us the list of these paragraphs?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I can read out the paragraphs right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: They're difficult for us to --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And we can hand you the numbered copies now, too, if you like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, we would need to see that, I think, with the passages marked on them, without reading them out now. Can you give the court officer a list of these?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I've got two other questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: One is, if we make you do this live, apart from the introductory part, the first 11 pages or so, what's it going to do to your time schedule?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Even if -- Your Honour, I think we estimated five hours. Even if you made me do the bulk of it live, I think it's going to be less than that because I will try my best to cut it down. We're already running way over this week and I want to get this witness done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, but some of this could be important evidence at this stage. There are things that we just have to take time with, unfortunately. The other question I have is this: Is Perisic likely to be a witness in this case?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Not at this stage, Your Honour, given his current circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So would you like me to provide you a list? On there I have not marked the paragraphs. I've only numbered them. I haven't marked the ones I would like --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, we do need a list of these numbers. Is the quickest way for you just to read it?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In full, I would omit paragraphs 70, 71, 97 -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: 112, 119, 126, 130, 134, 136, 141, and 142, 159 through 170, and 172. And I would also omit the last sentence of paragraph 97, the last paragraph of 116, the last sentence of 120, the last sentence of 126 and 153.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is this news to Mr. O'Sullivan?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I regret I wasn't here last evening when you wanted to address this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: This should not be regarded as an indication of a view because we haven't had a chance to look at these -- the statement with these passages removed. But, Mr. Hannis, we think that you should in any event produce a copy of this statement that omits all these passages, and you should overnight undertake that task -- or, I suppose you could wait until we wait a decision. But in any event, if it is a difficult exercise, please wait until we make a decision. But if we do decide to do it that way, we'd like a copy that omits all these passages. We'll make a decision tomorrow morning. We should be in a position to announce it when we come on to the bench. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So we'll resume at 9.00 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 10th day of November, 2006, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.15 p.m.,
